newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Treasury raises $42.4 mln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Treasury raises $42.4 mln in bonds.

text.p: Morocco's finance ministry said on Friday Public Treasury raised a total 390.5 million dirhams ($42.4 million) bonds on the Casablanca stock exchange.

"Public subscription for public Treasury bonds at between 8.5 and 9.5 percent interest rate raised a total 390.5 million dirhams against 443.5 million in the first quarter of 1996," a ministry official told Reuters.
Subscription was opened from 24 to 28 March 1997, the official said.
The Treasury bonds called "Emprunt National" are listed on the stock exchange as part of the state domestic debt oriented to small investors and are negotiable on the market.

"We noticed a slight drop in value of T-bond isssue raised on the bourse in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year because investors were focused on attractive profits of the bourse shares this year," a market analyst said.
The government bonds showed interest rates down 0.5 percent compared with the previous issue, the official added.
The bonds were issued as follows: one-year bond at 8.5 percent, three-year bond at 9.0 percent and five-year bond at 9.5 percent, a bourse spokesman said.

The bonds divided in tranches of 5,000 dirhams ($532) and 50,000 dirhams ($5,319) are open to the public and all operators including foreign institutions to stimulate the bond market, the spokesman added.

In the past, institutional investors were barred from access to public treasury bond issues, including insurance companies. But since September 1996, institutional investors have been allowed to subscribe to these bonds, officials said.
The government issues every three months public T-bonds and it was the second time it cut interest rates by 0.50 percent in a period of six months, a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
According to Bank al-Maghrib (central bank), public treasury bonds issue on the stock exchange dropped to 3.3 billion dirhams in the whole year of 1996 from 4.6 billion dirhams in 1995.
